summary.one_liner: A small C interpreter, written in C, that is able to interpret its own source code, with a step-by-step tutorial series.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains xc.c, a compact C interpreter based on c4 and rewritten for readability, and xc-tutor.c, a version written step by step for the accompanying tutorial. Running ./xc on a C file executes that program, and the -s flag is documented as a way to run it in the interpreter. The README shows that xc can run itself, e.g. ./xc xc.c hello.c, which is the "interprets itself" claim. The README also points to a tutorial series (in tutorial/en and a Chinese blog) that explains the lexer, recursive descent parser, and virtual machine design. A fork adding a debugger for xc.c is mentioned.
use_cases: learning how a C compiler or interpreter works
following a step-by-step compiler building tutorial
running small C programs without a full compiler toolchain
exploring a virtual machine for C-like code
notable: Interprets itself: xc.c can run xc.c, and can even run it twice nested
Based on c4 but rewritten for understandability
Includes xc-tutor.c written step by step for a tutorial
Accompanied by a multi-part tutorial series in English and Chinese
A fork adds a debugger for xc.c
caveats: The README does not describe the supported subset of C or the language features beyond the basics
No platform or compiler requirements beyond gcc are stated
The tutorial series is referenced by path and links, not included in the README text
